data.exact_reserve_text: 2015 year of account: Cumulative closing loss of GBP 4.0m (movement in CY 2017: profit of GBP 0.2m); Run-off years of account: 2014: cumulative closing loss of GBP 12.6m (movement in CY 2017: loss of GBP 1.3m); 2013: cumulative closing loss of GBP 8.4m (movement in CY 2017: loss of GBP 2.2m); 2012: cumulative closing loss of GBP 21.6m (movement in CY 2017: loss of GBP 4.4m).
specific_events: Reinsurance to Close (RITC) for 2012, 2013, 2014 years of account

prior_year_events.event_name: Reinsurance to Close (RITC) for run-off years
prior_year_events.impact_description: The 2012, 2013, and 2014 years of account were placed into run-off and subsequently subject to an external RITC agreement. The movement in CY 2017 for these years resulted in losses of GBP 4.4m, GBP 2.2m, and GBP 1.3m respectively, totaling a GBP 7.9m strengthening (net).
The 2015 year of account closed with a profit of GBP 0.2m in CY 2017, indicating a release of reserves (net).
Net claims of GBP 1.1m were released from the 2016 CAT event Hurricane Matthew as claims developed more favourably than anticipated.

named_events.loss_description: HUL entered into a RITC agreement for each run-off year (2012, 2013, 2014) to transfer assets and liabilities to Syndicate 3330's 2018 year of account.

Part of the 'HIM' losses, Harvey was the wettest tropical cyclone on record in the United States, causing floods in Texas. The net loss impact of HIM losses booked in the 2017 year of account is GBP 14.6m.
Part of the 'HIM' losses, Irma was a category five hurricane that struck the Leeward Islands and Florida. The net loss impact of HIM losses booked in the 2017 year of account is GBP 14.6m.

Part of the 'HIM' losses, Maria was a category five hurricane that struck the Leeward Islands and caused catastrophic damage in Puerto Rico. The net loss impact of HIM losses booked in the 2017 year of account is GBP 14.6m.
A further GBP 1.5m of net claims arose from the Mexico earthquake in September 2017.
Net losses of GBP 1.8m arising from the Peruvian floods in March 2017, affecting the 2016 year of account.
Net claims of GBP 1.1m were able to be released from the 2016 CAT event Hurricane Matthew as claims developed more favourably than anticipated.

data.standardized_narrative: The syndicate experienced a gross prior year reserve strengthening of GBP 5.129 million in 2017, primarily driven by adverse development on older underwriting years (2011-2014) as calculated from the gross claims development triangle. This was partially offset by a release on the 2015 underwriting year. The run-off years of account (2012, 2013, 2014) were subject to an external Reinsurance to Close (RITC) agreement, which involved a detailed due diligence exercise and recalibration of reserves, resulting in net losses for these years. The 2015 year of account showed a net profit movement. Additionally, the 2016 year of account saw a net release of GBP 1.1m from Hurricane Matthew claims, while also being impacted by net losses from the 2017 HIM hurricanes and Peruvian floods.
raw_causal_phrases: on-going uncertainty over the final loss arising from a combination of factors, the most material being continuing assessment of the reserving position due to volatility experienced
reserving uncertainty was compounded by the slow earning profile of this year of account with some residual exposure live in to 2017

risks which led to the years of account being left in run-off were suitably reduced and approved an independently managed competitive tender process be undertaken to facilitate an external reinsurance to close (RITC)

The 2015 business plan was compiled by the managing agency pre change of control on 1 April 2015. The only business written to this year of account comprised a Canadian sports binder incepting February 2015, a small open market contingency book of business and business written via the Lloyd's China reinsurance platform. As a consequence of the very limited business written together with start-up costs in respect of the Hamilton business, the year will close with a loss of GBP 4.0m, which is in line with our expectations.

no sensitivity analysis has been performed as the run-off years have been reserved at the premium they are transferring to the external RITC provider at and the 2015 year of account reserves are not material.
claims developed more favourably than anticipated

gross_premium_mix.line_of_business: Fire and other damage of property

data.data_quality_notes: The prior year development figure is calculated from the gross claims development triangle. The report mentions a Reinsurance to Close (RITC) for the 2012, 2013, and 2014 years of account effective 31 December 2017, which may distort the interpretation of movements in the claims triangle for these years. Narrative text on page 4 provides net movements for these run-off years and the 2015 year of account, which sum to a net strengthening of GBP 7.7m, differing from the gross triangle calculation.
